title: The frozen commodity
text: {{1}} the early nineteenth century, shipping frozen water to the tropics sounded like a joke, and the whole plan {{2}} openly ridiculed. Frederic Tudor, a Boston merchant {{3}} stubbornness became legendary, was convinced otherwise. He shipped his first cargo of New England lake ice {{4}} the Caribbean in 1806, and most of it {{5}} indeed melted long before arrival. {{6}} insulating the blocks in sawdust and building proper icehouses at both ends, he steadily cut his losses, and by the 1830s ice from Massachusetts ponds was {{7}} great a fixture in southern cities that hot climates came to depend on it. Not until mechanical refrigeration spread in the twentieth century {{8}} the trade finally fade away.

gaps.explanation: Past passive with a singular subject: was ridiculed.
'Whose' links the merchant to his stubbornness.

gaps.hint: preposition: shipped his first cargo ___ the Caribbean
auxiliary: most of it ___ melted long before
gaps.explanation: Past perfect: the melting happened before the arrival.

gaps.hint: preposition: ___ insulating the blocks in sawdust
gaps.explanation: 'By + gerund' expresses the means of cutting losses.

gaps.hint: adverb: was ___ great a fixture that
gaps.explanation: 'So great a … that' — the inverted degree structure.

gaps.hint: auxiliary: not until refrigeration ___ the trade fade
gaps.explanation: Inversion after 'not until': 'did' carries the past tense.
